title_en: Xuzhou Xiyuan Yijun Garden (Phase I) Owners' Committee v. Xuzhou Zhongchuan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over confirmation of ownership of property management premises
ruling_gist_en: An owners' committee established in accordance with Article 75, Paragraph 1 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China possesses a certain purpose, name, organizational structure, and premises, and manages corresponding property; it constitutes an 'other organization' as defined in Article 49, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Where an owners' committee, based on a common decision of the owners or a resolution of the owners' assembly, engages in legal acts within the scope of its authorization in the name of the owners' committee, it has standing to sue.
keywords_en: civil; dispute over confirmation of real rights; first instance; basic people's court; Jiangsu Province; legal person; other organization; Property Law; Civil Procedure Law; standing of owners' committee; ownership of property management premises; effect of planning changes; in favor of plaintiff; planning changes for property management premises; owners' committee filing lawsuit; administrative reconsideration revoking planning changes; real rights; administrative litigation; dispute over confirmation of ownership of property management premises
full_text_en:
Xuzhou Xiyuan Yijun Garden (Phase I) Owners Committee v. Xuzhou Zhongchuan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Confirmation of Ownership of Property Management Premises

[Ruling Summary]

An owners committee established in accordance with paragraph 1 of Article 75 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, which has a specific purpose, name, organizational structure, and premises, and manages corresponding property, constitutes an "other organization" as defined in paragraph 1 of Article 49 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Where an owners committee engages in legal acts in its own name, within the scope of authorization by the common decision of the owners or by the resolution of the owners' assembly, it has standing to sue.

Property management premises, built in accordance with a designated planning location, are necessary premises for the management and maintenance activities of the manager of the condominium building. Pursuant to paragraph 1 of Article 72 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, such premises are jointly owned by the owners. After the building has been completed, accepted, and delivered, the division, transfer, adjustment, or reallocation of property management premises shall be decided by the common decision of the owners or by the owners' assembly.

Plaintiff: Xuzhou Xiyuan Yijun Garden (Phase I) Owners Committee, domiciled at Yijun Garden Community, No. 369 Huanghe South Road, Quanshan District, Xuzhou, Jiangsu Province.
Responsible Person: Hou Lishen, Chairperson of the Committee.

Defendant: Xuzhou Zhongchuan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 1417, Fanya Building, Xuzhou, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Sun Yong, Chairman of the Board.

The Plaintiff, Xuzhou Xiyuan Yijun Garden (Phase I) Owners Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Yijun Owners Committee"), filed a lawsuit with the Quanshan District People's Court of Xuzhou City against the Defendant, Xuzhou Zhongchuan Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Zhongchuan Company"), regarding a dispute over the confirmation of ownership of property management premises.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The Yijun Garden (Phase I) located at No. 369 Huanghe South Road, Quanshan District, Xuzhou, is a residential community developed and constructed by the Defendant, Zhongchuan Company, in 2000. Upon delivery in August 2001, the Defendant only provided two garages for property management use. Later, it came to the Plaintiff's attention that the 168 square meter house on the east side of Building #8, which the Defendant had leased to others for operation of a kindergarten, was originally the property management premises for this community. In August 2008, when the Plaintiff sued requesting the Defendant to deliver the property management premises, the Defendant presented planning modification procedures showing that the property management premises had been changed to commercial premises. In December 2008, the Plaintiff filed an administrative reconsideration with the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government, requesting revocation of the aforementioned planning change decision made by the Xuzhou Planning Bureau. The Defendant subsequently filed an administrative lawsuit against this. After trials by the Xuzhou Intermediate People's Court and the Jiangsu High People's Court, the judgments both upheld the reconsideration decision of the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government. After the judgments took effect, the parties failed to reach an agreement on the delivery of the property management premises. Therefore, the Plaintiff filed this lawsuit, requesting the court to confirm that the 168 square meters of property management premises located on the east side of Building #8, Yijun Garden, No. 369 Huanghe South Road, Quanshan District, Xuzhou (as specified in the planning site plan) are owned jointly by all owners of Xuzhou Xiyuan Yijun Garden (Phase I), and that the litigation costs be borne by the Defendant.

Defendant's Defense: 1. The original plaintiffs in this case were all owners of Xuzhou Xiyuan Yijun Garden (Phase I), constituting a class action. At the time of filing, the Xuzhou Yijun Garden Owners Committee had already been established. Therefore, the all-owners' plaintiff group lacked proper standing, and their lawsuit should be withdrawn or dismissed according to law. 2. As supporting facilities, property management premises were not mandatory before 2000. The Yijun Garden community in question was designated in the planning site plan in 1997, construction commenced in June 2000, and it passed inspection on August 29, 2001. After delivery of the houses, the Defendant entered into a property management entrustment contract with a property management company and transferred the relevant premises to that company for use as property management premises, thereby fulfilling the Defendant's obligations as the developer. Therefore, absent mandatory regulations on property management premises at that time, the Defendant had fulfilled its contractual or customary obligations. The property management premises designated in the 1997 planning site plan were designed for the total construction area of 110,500 square meters shown in the plan, whereas the Plaintiff's community covers only 21,403 square meters. According to the Jiangsu Province Property Management Regulations, the Defendant would, at most, need to deliver 85.6 square meters of property management premises to the Plaintiff to comply with legal requirements. 3. The planning site plan records commercial premises and property management premises, but the location marked "commercial" in the plan is not necessarily the commercial premises, and the location marked "property management" is not necessarily the property management premises; rather, the premises have two floors used for both commercial and property management purposes. How to specifically allocate them should be decided by the Defendant, as long as it meets the basic legal requirements. 4. Given the current state of the premises, delivering the second floor of the disputed premises to the Plaintiff would satisfy both the Plaintiff's requirements and the legal provisions.

Facts Found by the Court: The Quanshan District People's Court of Xuzhou City found the following through trial: The Defendant, Zhongchuan Company, was the developer of the Xuzhou Xiyuan Yijun Garden (Phase I) community where the Plaintiff, Yijun Owners Committee, is located. On June 21, 2000, the Defendant obtained the Land Use Planning Permit (Xushiguidi (2000) No. 81) from the Xuzhou Planning Bureau. The planning site plan designated the property management premises for Xiyuan Yijun Garden (Phase I) as follows: 2 floors (height limit 6 meters), with a property management area of 260 square meters. On November 15, 2000, the Xuzhou Planning Bureau issued the Construction Project Planning Permit (Xushiguijian (2000) No. 268) for the Xiyuan Yijun Garden project constructed by the Defendant, approving the construction of 7 six-story residential buildings (total area 21,403 square meters), garages (3,006 square meters), lofts (3,322 square meters), commercial premises (2,032 square meters), and property management premises, public restrooms, and pump rooms (300 square meters), totaling 30,063 square meters. The permit's attached drawings and the "Setting-out (Inspection) Receipt" designated specific locations for the aforementioned buildings. The planning site plan authorized by the Xuzhou Planning Bureau divided Building #8 of Yijun Garden into three parts, from east to west: Property Management (2 floors, height limit 6 meters, east-west length 12 meters, north-south width 7 meters), Commercial (1 floor, east-west length 6 meters), and Public Restroom (1 floor, east-west length 10 meters). The specific distribution was: the area of the property management premises was 12×7×2 = 168 square meters; the pump room area was 8×5 = 40 square meters; the restroom area (trapezoidal) was [(7+3)\2]×10 = 50 square meters, totaling 258 square meters of property management premises. On August 30, 2001, the Xuzhou Construction Bureau issued the Residential Completion Acceptance Certificate (Xujianyanzheng (27) No.) for the Defendant's construction project. The Defendant immediately delivered the houses and notified the owners of Xiyuan Yijun Garden (Phase I) to take possession. Subsequently, the Defendant submitted a "Report on the Application for Change of Use of Zhongchuan 'Yijun Garden' Building #8" to the Xuzhou Planning Bureau, requesting that most of the property management premises in Building #8 (as planned in November 2000) be changed to commercial premises, while maintaining the original planned area, and setting up a commensurate area of property management premises on the ground floor of the west side of Building #7. On November 6, 2001, the Xuzhou Planning Bureau noted on the original planning site plan: "Approved to change 126 square meters of original property management premises to commercial premises." On the same day, the Bureau issued the Construction Project Planning Permit (Xushiguijian 20010214 No.) to the Defendant, authorizing the construction of 126 square meters of commercial premises. On November 7, 2001, relevant responsible persons of the Xuzhou Planning Bureau respectively signed on the Defendant's "Application Form for Construction Project Planning Permit of Xuzhou City": "Approved the adjustment. The area of property management premises shall not be less than the originally designated area" and "Approved." The modified plan showed that two rooms for property management, recorded as 28.45 square meters and 22.67 square meters respectively, were retained on the second floor of Building #8. After the completion and delivery of the Xiyuan Yijun Garden houses, the Defendant delivered, and the Plaintiff has used to date, property management premises consisting of two rooms on the ground floor of the west side of Building #7 and two rooms on the ground floor of Building #4, all of which were originally within the scope of the planned garages.

It was further found that in December 2008, all owners of Xuzhou Xiyuan Yijun Garden (Phase I) filed an administrative reconsideration with the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government, requesting the revocation of the administrative act of the Xuzhou Planning Bureau which "changed the planned 126 square meters of property management premises in Xuzhou Xiyuan Yijun Garden (Phase I) to commercial premises, and changed the same area of garages on the west side of Building #7 to property management premises." On March 4, 2009, the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government issued the Administrative Reconsideration Decision [(2008) Xuxingfu No. 146], deciding to revoke the specific administrative act of the Xuzhou Planning Bureau as described above. On April 22, 2009, the Defendant, Zhongchuan Company, dissatisfied with the aforementioned reconsideration decision, filed an administrative lawsuit with the Xuzhou Intermediate People's Court, requesting the revocation of the reconsideration decision and the affirmation of the administrative act of the Xuzhou Planning Bureau. After trial, the Xuzhou Intermediate People's Court rendered the Administrative Judgment [(2009) Xuxingchuzi No. 23] on June 16, 2009, dismissing the Defendant's claims. The Defendant appealed to the Jiangsu High People's Court. The Jiangsu High People's Court rendered the Administrative Judgment [(2009) Suxingzhongzi No. 79] on November 27, 2009, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

It was later found that on January 17, 2003, the Xuzhou Real Estate Management Bureau registered the property at Building #8, Yijun Garden, No. 369 Huanghe South Road, Quanshan District, Xuzhou (including the disputed property management premises, but excluding the west side of the building planned as a public restroom) in the name of the Defendant, Zhongchuan Company. The Property Ownership Certificate shows a first-floor construction area of 135.28 square meters and a second-to-third-floor construction area of 165.9 square meters. The property file shows that the east section of Building #8, comprising two floors, measures 12 meters east-west and 7 meters north-south.

On March 5, 2013, the court organized an on-site inspection of Building #8 of Yijun Garden, the subject of this case, with both parties present. It was confirmed that Building #8 is currently leased by the Defendant, Zhongchuan Company, and used as a kindergarten. Its appearance is divided into three parts: the east side has two floors, the middle has three floors, and the west side has one floor. There are simple staircases leading to the second floor on the east and north sides of the building.

The plaintiff at the time of case filing was "all owners of Xuzhou Xiyuan Yijun Garden (Phase I)." Subsequently, upon the plaintiff's application, the plaintiff entity was changed to the "Xuzhou Xiyuan Yijun Garden (Phase I) Owners Committee."

The disputed issues in this case between the two parties are: 1. Whether the Yijun Owners Committee has standing as plaintiff; 2. What effect the administrative planning designation has on the parties in this case; 3. What is the validity of the Defendant Zhongchuan Company's reallocation of the property management premises; 4. Whether the disputed building is classified as property management premises or commercial premises.

Opinion of the Court: The Quanshan District People's Court of Xuzhou City held as follows after trial:

1. The Yijun Owners Committee has proper standing as plaintiff. According to Article 40 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the term "other organizations" in Article 49 of the Civil Procedure Law refers to organizations that are lawfully established, have certain organizational structures and property, but do not have legal personality. The Plaintiff was established to manage Xiyuan Yijun Garden in accordance with paragraph 1 of Article 75 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China. Having a specific purpose, name, organizational structure, and premises, managing corresponding property, and represented by a specific representative externally, it constitutes an "other organization" as defined in paragraph 1 of Article 49 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Based on the common decision of the owners or the resolution of the owners' assembly, and within the authorized scope, the Plaintiff, using its own name as the owners committee, asserts a real claim against the Defendant for confirmation of ownership of the property management premises in accordance with Article 14 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues concerning the Specific Application of Law in Trials of Disputes over Condominium Ownership. Thus, it has standing to sue.

2. The administrative planning designation has binding force on the parties in this case. The planning designation of a building construction determines specific matters such as the building's location, scope, public facility area, and burden rate. According to Article 32 of the Urban Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, for construction, expansion, or renovation of buildings, structures, roads, pipelines, and other engineering facilities within a planned urban area, the relevant approval documents must be submitted to the urban planning administrative department for application. The department will issue a construction project planning permit based on the planning design requirements set forth in the urban plan. An construction unit or individual may only apply for construction commencement procedures after obtaining the construction project planning permit and other relevant approvals. A designated planning location constitutes an administrative licensing act that determines the rights and obligations of the land user before construction commences. If the land user does not object to the designated planning location within a specific period, it becomes binding on them. In this case, the Defendant, Zhongchuan Company, did not object to the designated planning location after receiving the construction project planning permit from the administrative authority. Therefore, the Defendant was obligated to construct the property management premises in accordance with the designated planning location. The Defendant's argument that the property management premises were designed for the total construction area of 110,500 square meters in the planning drawings, rather than for the 21,403 square meters community of the Plaintiff, Yijun Owners Committee, was not supported by evidence and was therefore rejected. The Defendant further argued that, according to the Jiangsu Province Property Management Regulations, which require providing 3‰-4‰ of the design area free of charge for property management premises, it was obliged to deliver at most 85.6 square meters to the Plaintiff, and the premises already provided far exceeded this standard. Because the Defendant did not raise any objection to the administrative authority when applying for the construction project planning permit and the authority approved the designated planning location, it is deemed that the Defendant accepted the authority's designated planning location. Therefore, this argument was also rejected. After the building is completed, accepted, and delivered, the designated planning location, transferred as part of the property management documents, becomes part of the management rules and is binding on the owners, manager, and others.

3. The Defendant Zhongchuan Company's reallocation of the property management premises is invalid due to illegality. Article 38 of the "Jiangsu Province Urban Residential Area Property Management Measures," promulgated and effective on September 4, 1998, by the Jiangsu Provincial People's Government, provides: "The development and construction unit of a residential area shall construct property management premises in accordance with relevant regulations and shall, at the time of overall handover of the residential area, hand them over to the owners committee of the residential area. The property rights of the property management premises belong to all owners of the residential area." Article 26 of the "Jiangsu Province Property Management Regulations," enacted by the Standing Committee of the Jiangsu Provincial People's Congress and effective from March 1, 2001, also clearly stipulates: "When planning and constructing new properties, necessary supporting facilities for property management shall be built, and a property management implementation plan shall be formulated and filed with the property management administrative department. After completion, the property management administrative department shall conduct an acceptance inspection of the property management supporting facilities. The property rights of the property management service premises belong to all owners of the residential area." Article 22 of the "Interim Measures of Xuzhou City for Urban Residential District Property Management," promulgated and implemented by the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government on March 31, 1999, provides: "The development and construction unit shall construct property management premises in accordance with planning requirements and shall, at the time of overall handover of the residential area, hand over the property management premises to the owners committee of the residential area. If an owners committee has not yet been established, the premises shall be handed over to the property management administrative department. The property rights of the property management premises belong to all owners of the residential area, and the premises shall be used by the property management enterprise. No unit or individual shall transfer the property management premises without authorization or change the nature of their use." According to the above provisions, after the Xuzhou Construction Bureau issued the Residential Completion Acceptance Certificate (Xujianyanzheng (27) No.) on August 30, 2001, and the Plaintiff immediately notified the owners to take possession, the property management premises in question became, by law, jointly owned by all owners of Xiyuan Yijun Garden (Phase I). In this case, after the completion, acceptance, and delivery of Xiyuan Yijun Garden, the Defendant, Zhongchuan Company, had no right to dispose of the property management premises. Its application to the administrative department for a change of the property management premises violated Article 71 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and is therefore null and void.

4. The property in dispute in this case should be confirmed as property management premises. Although the Xuzhou Planning Bureau approved on November 7, 2001, the change of most of the originally planned property management premises to commercial premises, and the change of the same area of garages on the west side of Building #7 to property management premises, and issued a construction project planning permit accordingly, such a change required the consent of all owners of Xiyuan Yijun Garden. The Xuzhou Planning Bureau's approval of the change without the owners' consent constituted an abuse of power. Because this planning change was revoked by the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government, the status quo ante must be restored. An analysis of the original planning site plan in this case shows that the planned property management premises for the Yijun Garden community should be the 168-square-meter two-floor section on the east side of Building #8. The Defendant, Zhongchuan Company, argued that it had already provided two garages each in Buildings #4 and #7 as property management premises, meeting the needs of all owners of Xiyuan Yijun Garden. Property management premises are necessary premises for the manager to manage the living environment and to meet the owners' needs for a safe, healthy, convenient, and comfortable living environment. Their division, transfer, adjustment, or reallocation, pursuant to Article 76, paragraph 1, item (7) of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, requires a resolution of the owners' assembly. Therefore, the Defendant's further argument that its reallocation of property management premises, by using some garages as property management premises of equivalent area for the Plaintiff's use, already satisfied the Plaintiff's actual needs, can only be considered the Defendant's own opinion. Such an action, which reduces the Plaintiff's other interests such as parking needs to compensate for the necessity of having property management premises, actually infringes upon the Plaintiff's interests and is improper. As the Defendant provided no evidence to support that it had indeed satisfied the Plaintiff's interests, this argument was also rejected.

In conclusion, the Plaintiff, Yijun Owners Committee's request to confirm that the property management premises located on the east side of Building #8, Yijun Garden, No. 369 Huanghe South Road, Quanshan District, Xuzhou, as recorded in the planning site plan attached to the Construction Project Planning Permit (Xushiguijian (2000) No. 268), are jointly owned by all owners of Xuzhou Xiyuan Yijun Garden (Phase I), and its request to transfer the ownership registration of the disputed building, are legally supported and should be granted.

Pursuant to paragraph 1 of Article 49 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China; Article 40 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China; Articles 33 and 73 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China; and Article 14 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues concerning the Specific Application of Law in Trials of Disputes over Condominium Ownership, the Quanshan District People's Court of Xuzhou City rendered the following judgment on December 16, 2013:

It is confirmed that the property management rooms located on the east side (two floors) of Building 8#, Yijun Garden, No. 369 Huanghe South Road, Quanshan District, Xuzhou City (as recorded in the site plan of the Construction Engineering Planning Permit No. XuShiGuiJian (2000) 268) are owned jointly by all owners of Xuzhou Xiyuan Yijun Garden (Phase I).

After the judgment was rendered at first instance, neither party filed an appeal within the statutory period, and this judgment has become legally effective.
